clue.text: Trace the damaged tube

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tracks down a broken pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges TRACETHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical catheter is a thin flexible pipe inserted into the body.

clue.text: Fallout from bombshell ruined her plans

indicators.note: plans that are ruined are wrecked, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Fallout from shocking news wrecked a woman's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges HERPLANS. 'Bombshell' reads as shocking news but here is a literal shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragments of metal scattered by an exploding shell are what it throws out.

clue.text: Effect of quavers on the score

definitions.text: Effect of quavers on the score

parts.words: Effect of quavers on the score
parts.note: quavers are both short notes and trembles, so a trembling effect written in a musical score

explanation.surface: Seems to ask how short notes affect a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quavers' as trembles rather than eighth notes gives the musical wavering effect.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical term names a wavering, trembling effect produced by rapid repetition or pitch variation.

clue.text: Concealed layer swallows did for building

indicators.note: one thing swallowing another takes it inside

parts.note: a hen is a bird that lays eggs

indicators.note: building puts things together in a new shape, so the letters of did are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hidden layer devoured what was done for construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' is the anagram signal for the three letters of 'did', and 'layer' means an egg-laying bird, not a stratum.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something kept out of sight, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: One runs daily or perhaps weekly

definitions.text: One runs daily or perhaps weekly

parts.words: One runs daily or perhaps weekly
parts.note: a person who runs, that is manages, a daily newspaper or a weekly magazine

explanation.surface: Sounds like a jogger who exercises every day or once a week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' and 'weekly' are publications, and 'runs' means manages.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper or magazine runs the publication.

clue.text: Awfully wet, raw now — hide for time when the elements are more favourable

definitions.text: time when the elements are more favourable

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of the four words are mixed up

explanation.surface: In nasty wet, raw weather, someone takes cover until conditions improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges WETRAWNOWHIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief spell of suitable conditions, such as for a launch or climb, is this phrase.

clue.text: The new stadium designed for the team

indicators.note: a stadium designed is laid out anew, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh ground built for a football side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges THENEWSTADIUM. The clue is apt: this London football club moved to the new Olympic Stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a London football club, so it is an example of a sports side.

clue.text: It's audible although surprisingly I won't hear this

indicators.note: surprisingly signals an unexpected outcome, so the letters of the four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A paradox: something can be heard, yet the speaker claims they won't hear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges IWONTHEARTHIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being close enough to be heard means a sound is audible to the listener.

clue.text: A way ham is carved leading to complaint

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: a ham that is carved is cut up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Slicing a ham in a certain manner brings on an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is carved' rearranges HAM to HMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment, and this breathing disorder is one example.

clue.text: Press and TV ignoring a gallery's muse

indicators.note: ignoring the letter a means leaving it out of the word for press and TV

parts.note: newspapers and television together are the media
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: The press and television overlook a gallery's source of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops the final A from MEDIA. 'Muse' looks like a noun but is the verb. The Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or reflect quietly, a synonym for thinking deeply.

clue.text: In favour of short concert being curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means having the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a prom is short for a promenade concert

explanation.surface: Supporting a brief performance that gets cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being curtailed' removes the M of PROM. The Proms are a famous British summer concert series.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin preposition meaning for, used in English to mean supporting something.

clue.text: Go very pale, have to leave northern port

indicators.note: the word have is made to leave, that is taken out of the port's name

parts.note: Whitehaven is a port in Cumbria, north-west England

explanation.surface: Someone goes pale on being told to quit a northern harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes HAVE out of WHITEHAVEN. Whitehaven is a harbour town in Cumbria, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To blanch or lose colour, becoming pale or white, is the sense of the verb here.

clue.text: Bird's come down by train

parts.note: to land is to come down to earth
travelling by train is travelling by rail

explanation.surface: A bird has arrived by train.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the corncrake, a bird of the rail family.

clue.text: Most of musical act expected to arrive

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the word for musical act

parts.note: a duet is a musical performance by two

explanation.surface: Most of a show's performers are expected soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last letter T of DUET.
explanation.definitionFit: A train or guest that is scheduled to come at a given time is said to be this.

clue.text: Gem of an isle?

parts.note: a green gemstone that also names the island of Ireland in a well-known nickname

explanation.surface: Asks for a jewel belonging to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emerald Isle is a traditional name for Ireland, for its green landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A green precious stone, which also gives Ireland its poetic nickname.

clue.text: Drink, light, with no head

indicators.note: with no head means the first letter of the word for light is removed

parts.note: pale means light in colour

explanation.surface: A light drink with no froth on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no head' drops the P of PALE. 'Head' looks like a beer's froth.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of beer, so it is an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Am in control to bring about vessel

indicators.note: in places am inside the word for control

parts.note: to steer is to control direction

explanation.surface: Someone in charge sets about bringing a ship round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring about' is only a link to the definition, though it reads as turning a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship driven by steam power is a type of boat or vessel.

clue.text: Go and fish in way that costs money

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
a pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Going fishing somewhere you have to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is the noun meaning a turn, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll road, chiefly in American usage, where drivers must pay to travel along it.

clue.text: A bird with mother somewhere in Egypt

parts.note: a swan is a large water bird
a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A bird and its mother are spotted somewhere in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: A major dam across the Nile in southern Egypt, so it is a location there.

clue.text: Allude to note duplicated for judge

parts.note: to refer to something is to allude to it

indicators.note: duplicated means the note letter appears twice

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Mentioning a copied memo to a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duplicated' doubles E to EE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports official who adjudicates play is one who judges matters.

clue.text: Grow in line

parts.note: a crease is a fold line, or the line marked at cricket

explanation.surface: Develop while staying in step.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow is to become larger, a synonym for getting bigger.

clue.text: Renounce Frenchman, say, that's put inside

indicators.note: put inside means the letters for say are placed within the Frenchman's name

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name
e.g. is short for for example, which say means

explanation.surface: Disown a Frenchman who has been jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put inside' reads as slang for imprisoned but is the container signal; 'say' gives the abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back on a promise or deny a commitment is to break one's word.

clue.text: I love Latin — with English graduate, it's an elementary thing

parts.note: amo is Latin for I love
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A scholar loving Latin, with an English degree, calls something basic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elementary' here means simple in structure rather than easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled organism is about as simple a life form as there is.

clue.text: Recompense for fighting whilst overdrawn?

indicators.note: whilst means during, so the fighting happens within the word for overdrawn

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Payment for going into battle while broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whilst' acts as the container signal; an overdrawn account is said to be 'in the red'.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment given in return for service or effort is a synonym for compensation.

clue.text: Part of Okefenokee Swamp

indicators.note: part of means a run of letters taken from inside the place name

explanation.surface: Describes a section of a famous American wetland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Okefenokee is a vast swamp in Georgia and Florida, so the surface is accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: A low marshy area of waterlogged land, especially in eastern England.

clue.text: Phaetons, unsteady transport

indicators.note: unsteady suggests wobbling around, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Light carriages make a wobbly means of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsteady' rearranges PHAETONS. A phaeton is itself a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A light open horse-drawn carriage, an old-fashioned means of getting around.

clue.text: Forceful yet feeble boxing companion

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the companion is held inside

parts.note: puny means weak or feeble
CH is short for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A weakling boxer has a strong partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport but is the container signal; CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigorous and having impact, as in a style of writing that hits hard.

clue.text: Right pickle to follow small first bite

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
breakfast is the first meal of the day

explanation.surface: A pickle eaten after a small snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' means utter, as in 'a right mess'; British slang for a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a total mess or muddle, a synonym for a real shambles.
